### S02.07

**Question:** Approve a matrix for viewing, creating, editing, approving, signing, releasing, exporting and archiving each record type. Where must administrative authority stop short of clergy authority?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:310](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:310). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Priest, Parish Admin and secretary can prepare sacramental paperwork. The priest decides acceptance/approval. The secretary may record the priest's prior approval given outside the system; it takes effect without waiting for the priest to log in and must be logged and visible to him. This preserves decision D005.

**Sacramental workflow rules:**

1. Assigned priests, Parish Admins and secretaries can enter/precheck request information, collect supporting documents and prepare paperwork within their permitted parish scope. Draft preparation does not itself establish sacramental acceptance or an approved register entry.
2. A qualified, assigned priest makes the relevant ecclesiastical decision and may enter it directly.
3. A secretary acting on a specific priest's already-given instruction can use **Record priest's approval** for the authorized decision on that case. No prior digital instruction/delegation or repeat online approval is required to make this offline instruction usable.
4. The secretary uses their own account and selects the authorizing priest from eligible appointments. Record the case, exact decision/stage, secretary, priest, actual entry timestamp and brief instruction note. Capture when/how the instruction was received where known; never invent a date or rewrite entry history to make it look like the priest clicked.
5. Require an explicit statement such as **The named priest has already instructed me to record this decision for this request.** This confirms an actual case instruction, not an independent secretary decision or open-ended permission to approve all cases.
6. History states **Approved on behalf of Fr. [Name] by [Secretary]**. Priest-side activity and a notification identify the action and link to the record. Applicant-facing status can say **Approved by the parish priest** without exposing internal instruction notes.
7. The approval is effective when recorded. The priest's later reading/acknowledgment is visibility and oversight, not a second pending approval gate. An unread notification does not invalidate the approval.
8. The priest can flag an action recorded without authority or with incorrect details. Proposed correction uses a visible review/correction entry and appropriate suspension of any uncompleted dependent work; it does not erase history or silently undo a completed official record, signature or release. Exact dispute/correction rules need the detailed sacramental workflow specification.
9. Parish Admins and higher administrators do not automatically gain secretary-on-behalf approval through preparation access. Extending that capability needs an explicit separate decision. A bishop decision is not implied by a priest's instruction.
10. Approval, official-register approval, signing, issuance and release are distinct. The current user decision does not authorize secretaries to apply a priest's signature or bypass any later ecclesiastical review. Define which decision stages support on-behalf recording in S12–S14 before finalizing those controls.

**Proposed action meanings and boundaries:**

| Action | Required meaning in the permission matrix |
| --- | --- |
| View | Read the permitted record/fields at its actual scope; search, counters and previews obey the same privacy limits |
| Create | Start a draft/request, without implicitly approving it or creating authority |
| Edit | Change permitted fields at that stage; locked official facts use a correction workflow |
| Approve | Make or explicitly record a permitted decision with prerequisites, actor and responsible authority |
| Sign | Apply a signature under an independently defined signing permission; not inherited from data entry or proxy approval |
| Release | Give the intended recipient access to an already authorized final document; not another way to sign/approve it |
| Export/print | Take an authorized scope and field subset outside the screen; view permission alone need not imply bulk export |
| Archive | End active operational use while preserving required records and links; never a hidden synonym for permanent deletion |

**Proposed starting matrix for non-sacramental records and remaining actions:** The table completes the missing breadth of S02.07 but is not yet the owner's approved detailed matrix. “Office staff” below means the priest/Parish Admin/secretary or explicitly authorized scoped office administrator, not every staff account.

| Record type | View/create/edit | Decision or reserved action | Export/archive boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public parish profile/content | Authorized office editors; public sees published approved fields only | Authorized publisher; bishop/diocese controls organizational facts and appointments | Public output only; drafts/history stay restricted |
| Diocese/parish organization | Super Admin and scoped bishop/admin according to appointment | Organizational approval/activation under S02.02–S02.03; clergy office stays with ecclesiastical authority | Scoped administrative exports; active record-bearing parish closes/archives rather than cascades to deletion |
| Accounts and appointments | Own account details or permitted administrator functions; people cannot grant their own rank | Appointing authority per scope; protected changes under S02.13 | No credential export; revocation retains appointment history |
| People/households | Permitted office staff; own official record visible through member projection; finance/leader views only need their permitted subsets | Office identity/link/correction review; no self-approval of official correction | Scoped, field-limited exports; archive preserves linked official records |
| Parish membership/profile corrections | Applicant submits own proposal; office reviews evidence and proposed link/fields | Permitted office reviewer; requester cannot approve their own proposal | Avoid global account exposure; retain decision history |
| Sacramental request/preparation | Applicant's own projection plus authorized preparation staff | Priest decision or specific secretary-recorded priest decision above | Applicant sees own results; official bulk export needs explicit authority |
| Official register entry/correction | Permitted preparation and clergy views; approved facts protected | Assigned priest approves official entry; correction authority/process must be specified | No ordinary delete; corrections and historical entries remain attributable |
| Certificate/signature | Permitted preparation staff and clergy; applicant sees permitted own status/output | Priest approval/signature; bishop review where separately required | Final file release only after applicable approval/signature/identity gates; no signature delegation assumed |
| Ministry/roster | Assigned leader and permitted office/clergy; member gets permitted own/group information | Join/departure rules in S18; confidential departure reason restricted | Scoped roster/attendance exports; departure keeps history |
| Calendar/service plans | Authorized office/clergy/leader within audience and event scope | Required publication or clergy/room approvals remain distinct from drafting | Export excludes private titles/details not permitted to viewer |
| Registrations/check-in | Assigned event/office users and own applicant data; medical/guardian fields restricted | Confirmation, consent, check-in, pickup and refunds have separate rules | Restrict participant exports; retain attendance/payment/incident history under policy |
| Reservations/equipment | Authorized requester and resource/office staff; other users see only permitted availability | Resource-specific confirmation/fees/cancellation authority | Do not export private applicant details through public availability |
| Giving/finance | Treasurer/authorized finance users; viewer read/report only; ordinary secretary has Office Expenses access rather than automatic full Finance | Named financial approver and separation of duties in S25; no self-second-approval | Financial close/correction rules; no silent deletion of approved history |
| Office Expenses | Permitted office staff and explicitly authorized finance roles | Approved allowance/expense/review rules; preparation role does not imply every financial approval | Scoped voucher/monthly export; correction/deletion rule to be agreed in S25 |
| Notes/messages/concerns/incidents | Author, recipients or explicitly assigned reviewers/handlers according to record type | No rank-based browse-all; reviewer conflicts and identity restrictions apply | No general export/archive right inherited from administrative rank |
| Audit | Scoped authorized reviewers with appropriate event visibility | Read-only history; corrections add events rather than edit the past | Audit export itself requires permission and must exclude secrets/private case content |

This matrix is a foundation for the full per-role/per-record view/create/edit/approve/sign/release/export/archive specification. Later sections must supply exact field, money, retention and stage rules; agreement to “all modules stay” is not approval of all current role permissions.

**Reviewed completion:** Proposed stage allow-list is acceptance, verified official-entry approval and certificate-preparation approval, each with a separate actual case instruction; competent clergy must approve the exact stage scope under U04. Actual signature, episcopal decision and recipient/file release remain independent rights. A disputed instruction suspends uncompleted dependencies, appends a correction and routes any already-issued/registered outcome through formal amendment; it does not erase history.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Secretary records actual prior priest instruction effectively once; no automatic signature/bishop/admin extension occurs.

### S02.08

**Question:** Which exact office duties may Parish Admins and higher administrators perform when there is no secretary? Guest document controls need to agree with this policy.

**Disposition:** Keep — preserve the explicit principle and apply the detailed rules below. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:363](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:363). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Parish Admins and higher administrators can perform secretary duties when no secretary exists.

**Proposed completion:** No-secretary operation is a supported normal configuration. The assigned priest can perform office preparation; an appointed Parish Admin or an authorized diocesan/system office administrator can perform intake, ordinary person/household work, membership/correction reviews, calendar and facility administration, event forms, registration support, document collection and other explicitly permitted secretary duties within scope.

Do not require a fake secretary account or a secretary appointment just to enable these functions. Role labels continue to show the person's actual role; support is not performed by impersonating a secretary. Requests route to the assigned office team or priest when the secretary list is empty, and one person holding several roles receives one relevant notification rather than duplicates.

Office fallback does not itself grant priest decisions, signatures, private pastoral access, concern access or full finance authority. Under the currently agreed rule, only an authorized secretary records a prior priest approval on his behalf; an administrator who must do that would need an explicit decision granting that capability or a genuine secretary appointment. The priest can instead record the approval directly. This separates the owner's broad office fallback from the specifically authorized on-behalf exception.

The UI should show who currently owns office work and allow explicit reassignment. Absence of a secretary must never silently change who signed or made a clergy decision.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** No-secretary office work completes through eligible priest/admin without fake secretary account or inherited signature.

### S02.09

**Question:** Which duties may a priest delegate, to whom, for what period and with what visible notice? Which actions must remain personal to that priest?

**Disposition:** Keep — preserve the explicit principle and apply the detailed rules below. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:375](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:375). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Delegation follows the priest's decision.

**Proposed completion:** The priest chooses eligible staff and task distribution within parish policy, but delegation must name the person, parish, duty, scope, effective period and any restrictions. The user sees a clear acting-on-behalf label where appropriate; an account password is never shared as a delegation method.

| Delegation type | Proposed handling |
| --- | --- |
| Routine preparation/office work | Assigned to eligible office staff within their standing role or explicit scoped task authorization |
| A specific approval already given by the priest outside the system | Secretary records the prior decision under S02.07; no required prior online delegation or second online approval |
| Temporary ongoing operational coverage | Explicit duties, start/end, responsible priest and review/revocation; never blanket all-parish/all-role power |
| Priest duties assigned to another priest | Qualified active priest appointment and the required ecclesiastical authorization; duty allocation recorded |
| Signature, independent sacramental decision, bishop decision, confidential-case access | No automatic inheritance from administrative delegation; separate permitted authority required |

A delegation cannot exceed the giver's authority or cross into an unassigned parish, unrelated ministry or private case. It ends when expired, revoked or incompatible with loss/suspension of the underlying appointment. History retains both the acting account and the relevant responsible authority.

The scope of the specific offline instruction may be one request or a clearly enumerated set; it is not permission to decide future cases. Emergency/absence rules must identify an eligible substitute rather than treating unavailable clergy as an excuse for unqualified independent approval.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Delegation names duty, scope, people and period and cannot exceed giver’s authority.

### S02.10

**Question:** When someone is absent, transferred, retired, suspended or deceased, who handles their pending approvals and assigned work?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:393](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:393). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Priest, Super Admin or secretary handles pending work, depending on the situation.

**Proposed completion:** Responsibility is transferred according to the kind of work, not merely to whoever is available:

- Office preparation and coordination can move to another authorized secretary/Parish Admin, eligible office administrator or priest.
- Ministry operations can move to a newly appointed/acting leader; unrelated leaders do not gain automatic access.
- Financial work moves to a permitted finance operator/approver, preserving independent-review rules.
- A decision requiring a priest moves to another qualified appointed priest. A secretary may record a prior genuine instruction under S02.07 but does not acquire the absent priest's independent judgment or signature.
- Head-priest/clergy vacancies and episcopal escalations go to the bishop or competent ecclesiastical authority. A temporary acting priest designation must be explicit.
- Super Admins coordinate technical access and reassignment under the proper authority; they do not become the replacement religious or financial decision-maker by being developers.

Before planned departure, show a handover list of open requests, approvals, events, reservations, assigned tasks, financial work and expiring delegations. Retain prior authorship and decisions; transfer only future responsibility/access. Unplanned suspension/death immediately removes applicable authority and routes unattended work to the proper authority for reassignment.

Private pastoral notes, private conversations and concern cases do not transfer with an ordinary work queue. Their own sharing/case rules apply. A former staff member may retain an ordinary member account if otherwise eligible. An instruction allegedly given before an appointment ended but entered later must be handled as a reviewed historical situation; it must not be used to exercise an expired appointment as current authority.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Handover transfers future eligible work while preserving authorship and private-case/notebook boundaries.

### S02.11

**Question:** What should happen to open forms and pending actions when access is revoked during a session? What explanation and safe destination should the user receive?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:410](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:410). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner response:** Recommendation requested.

**Recommended answer:** Revocation takes effect for the next protected read or write, including sessions already open. The affected appointment stops authorizing actions immediately; do not wait until the next login or show a success result for a rejected save.

The user receives a plain-language message such as **Your access to this parish or role has changed. Your last action was not completed.** The message identifies their own affected context and an appropriate contact without exposing confidential reasons or another person's account details.

Close/restrict unauthorized detail screens, refresh available workspaces and navigate to an allowed workspace, My account or sign-in as appropriate. Removing one parish assignment does not remove other parish appointments or the account's unrelated member access. Global deactivation ends all access.

For unsaved forms, do not complete a submission using revoked authority or upload a hidden recovery copy of restricted data. Preserve only a draft that the account is still permitted to retain; otherwise explain the failure and route recovery through an authorized colleague/support process. Sensitive information already delivered to a device cannot be assumed to have been unseen; the interface must stop further authorized access and remove it from ordinary active views.

If the operation committed before the revocation, preserve its original actor/time and show it as completed only after checking its actual state. If it did not commit, it remains incomplete. A failed response must not be interpreted as proof either way. The same rule applies when a delegation, case assignment, appointment expiry or parish deactivation changes access.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Revoked open session fails next protected action, accurately checks prior commit and offers safe permitted destination.

### S02.12

**Question:** Should appointments have start/end dates, invitation acceptance or periodic review? What should upcoming expiry look like to the appointee and administrator?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:424](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:424). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Appointments should have dates, acceptance and review features.

**Proposed completion:** Every assignment records role, organization/ministry scope, appointing authority, start date/time, status, lead designation where relevant and history. End date is optional for ongoing appointments and required for temporary cover. Distinguish a scheduled end from an earlier manual revocation.

Recommended statuses: **Invited/Pending acceptance**, **Scheduled**, **Active**, **Suspended**, **Expired**, **Declined** and **Revoked/Ended** as appropriate. The effective date and acceptance requirements must both be met before an ordinary invited assignment becomes usable. A first privileged-account setup or an officially recorded existing appointment may need an explicit controlled activation path; it must not be mislabeled as a privately accepted invitation.

An invitation explains the role, parish/diocese, duties and dates. The person can accept, decline or request correction using their own identity. Membership invitation, ministry membership and staff appointment are different processes.

**Proposed defaults:** Notify the appointee and appointing authority 30 days and 7 days before expiry, with a clear period/recipient configuration for short appointments. Review active staff/administrative appointments annually and when leadership changes. These intervals are proposed product defaults, not claimed church requirements. Any configured reminders must actually be deliverable through the chosen in-system/scheduled mechanism.

Renewal requires an explicit authorized action; expiry never silently extends itself. Display the exact end time and parish time zone. Review reminders should not terminate an indefinite assignment unless an explicit expiry/revocation rule says so. Provide an escalation path for a head-priest vacancy or inaccessible last administrator so continuity is not solved through invented credentials.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Accepted/effective appointment dates control authority; expiry/review reminders never silently extend a grant.

### S02.13

**Question:** Which administrative changes need a reason, a second approver or current-password confirmation, and how should the confirmation describe its exact effect?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:438](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:438). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner response:** No substantive answer supplied.

**Proposed answer:** Use safeguards appropriate to the effect of the action. A reason, current-password confirmation and a second person's approval are three different controls; requiring one does not satisfy the others.

| Change | Proposed safeguard |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary clerical correction/draft change | Standard permitted save and history; extra reasons only where the record/workflow requires them |
| Staff role grant/revocation, temporary delegation, lead change | Explicit target/scope/effective-date confirmation and recorded reason; appointing authority must be eligible |
| Super Admin grant/revocation or global account deactivation | Current-password confirmation, reason and confirmation by another active Super Admin; a request to remove access cannot leave the platform without a controlled active administrator |
| Initial first Super Admin / exceptional recovery | Distinct controlled setup/recovery process with audit; no impossible requirement for a second account before the first exists |
| First bishop appointment or diocesan reassignment | Verified real authority, reason, effective scope/date and review by another eligible platform administrator for the administrative action; this does not confer religious office |
| Parish creation/activation or change of responsible clergy | Relevant bishop approval/appointment and clear parish/lead-priest summary; local staff cannot self-promote into clergy |
| Parish closure, removal of an unused setup or organizational ownership change | Impact preview, reason, reauthentication and independent authorized review; record-bearing parishes do not use ordinary hard deletion |
| Password recovery for privileged account | Verify target identity, current-password confirmation for the acting authorized administrator, reason and revoke the recovered account's old sessions; never disclose the password in an activity log |
| Exceptional confidential access or private export | Purpose, precise permitted records, appropriate independent authorization and audit; no permanent browse-all capability created as a shortcut |

The two developer accounts should remain separately usable for ordinary dual-control actions. Proposed operational policy is to maintain at least two active Super Admins; if a planned removal reduces that number, establish a replacement first. A genuine compromise/recovery procedure must still be able to contain a compromised account rather than being blocked by this operating target. Protection against losing all active privileged access remains mandatory.

The confirmation must show **who/what changes, exact scope, effect on access and pending work, effective date and reversibility**. A person cannot be the independent second approver by switching roles or accounts under their sole control. Temporary protective suspensions may need immediate effect with subsequent review, rather than waiting while compromised access remains usable; define that exception and its reviewers explicitly.

This proposal does not introduce a second online priest approval for the specific secretary-recorded instruction in S02.07.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Reason, reauthentication and independent approval are separately enforced for each listed high-impact change.

### S02.14

**Question:** How should a user request missing access or challenge an incorrect appointment without seeing unauthorized records or other people's account details?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S01-S02-refined-answers.md:462](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S01-S02-refined-answers.md:462). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner response:** No answer supplied.

**Proposed answer:** Provide **Request access** and **Report incorrect appointment** from My account and appropriate denied-access screens. Requesting an appointment creates a review request; it never grants the requested role automatically.

Collect the requested organization, duty/role, reason, expected dates and the requester's own contact/account identity. Show only a public/authorized directory of target organizations and their own existing appointments; do not expose private staff lists, account matches, patient/person records or confidential case identifiers through an access request form.

Route parish staff requests to the head priest or eligible appointing authority, diocesan administrative requests to the bishop, and platform/bishop-onboarding issues to the Super Admin review process. Clergy appointment requests go through the ecclesiastical authority rather than ordinary office approval. Existing complaints about a conflicted authority follow an independent escalation route rather than being automatically disclosed to that same person.

Statuses should include **Submitted**, **Needs information**, **Approved/appointment offered**, **Declined**, **Withdrawn** and **Resolved** where applicable. A reviewer states scope/dates and an understandable outcome; the requester receives the result and a next action. Staff can decline their own pending invitation or report an incorrect active assignment without seeing anyone else's appointment details.

No reviewer approves their own request, appoints an unauthorized peer/superior or overrides independent-case restrictions. An escalation must go to an actually eligible authority. On approval, create the proper invitation/assignment and apply S02.12. Keep the access request and appointment history linked but distinct. General access appeals must not become a way to browse concern cases or private pastoral notes.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; competent appointing authority/bishop; head priest. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF38](workflow-specifications.md#wf38), [WF39](workflow-specifications.md#wf39); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s02). Scenario references: [A09](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a09), [A12](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a12), [A22](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a22), [A23](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a23), [A25](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a25), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Own access request routes to eligible authority without showing unrelated accounts, records or confidential cases.

## S03 — Navigation, dashboard, search and work queues

### S03.01

**Question:** What should be the first screen after login for each role, including an account with no parish, a follower without membership and an unassigned priest?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:15](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:15). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** An account with one available role enters its dashboard directly. An account with multiple available roles chooses the role it wants to use and then enters the dashboard. Do not skip this choice by automatically opening the last-used role. The account remains signed in when switching between its authorized roles.

The dashboard is the one combined home described in S03.02. It adapts to the selected role and includes the account's permitted personal/community information without requiring another home/workspace switch. An ordinary member identity does not by itself add a redundant role-choice step for someone with only one working role; exact role-choice presentation is a UX detail for validation.

People with no parish relationship can discover nearby/selected-area parishes and read publicly listed events and other published parish information. Location access is optional; locality/name search remains available. A follower without approved membership sees the parish's published events and public information, but following does not expose office records, private group content or other people's data.

An unassigned priest receives a clear **Awaiting parish assignment** state, with their own account information and public discovery still available. This is a pending state, not parish working access.

**Proposed refinements for additional account contexts:** The following table describes priorities inside the same combined home, not separate personal/work home screens. Detailed dashboard contents remain open under S03.07.

| Account/context | First destination and immediate purpose |
| --- | --- |
| First Super Admin, no organization yet | System Home with initialization steps: establish second privileged account, diocese and bishop appointment |
| Super Admin after initialization | System Home: organization status, authorized administration work and relevant access/support issues; no automatic private-record feed |
| Bishop | Diocese Home: parish overview, clergy/administrative matters and decisions actually requiring the bishop |
| Archdiocese Admin | Diocese Administration Home: permitted organization/office work and delegated responsibilities |
| Head or other assigned priest | Parish Home: requests requiring a priest, today's/upcoming calendar, office exceptions and actions recorded on his behalf |
| Parish Admin | Parish Office Home: intake, preparation, calendar/reservation/event issues and authorized administrative work |
| Secretary | Parish Office Home: today's calendar, requests to prepare/follow up, reservations and event registrations |
| Treasurer | Finance Home: actual finance work, reconciliation/approvals within authority and clearly dated balances |
| Finance viewer | Finance Overview: permitted summaries/reports, with viewing rather than transaction-entry actions |
| Ministry leader | Ministry Home: assigned ministries, meetings, membership reviews, attendance and volunteer work |
| Member with approved parish link | Personal Home: own requests, upcoming activities, messages and commitments |
| Account following parishes without membership | Personal Home with followed public activity, membership status and explicit next steps; no implied staff/person-record access |
| Account with no parish relationship | Personal Home with Find a parish, follow/choose primary parish and optional profile completion |
| Priest account with no current assignment | **Awaiting parish assignment** home state, own account information and public discovery; no parish records opened automatically |

A valid direct link received before login should return the user to the intended record after authentication, required role choice and access checking. A link must not silently select a privileged role or a different parish. A role must not force an ordinary account to redo completed onboarding on every login.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** One available role enters directly; multiple roles require choice; no-parish/follower/unassigned-priest states remain useful.

### S03.02

**Question:** Should staff enter their work tools and personal parish life through one switch, separate destinations, or one combined home? Confirm the current exclusion of secretary personal member routes.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:46](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:46). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Provide **one combined home** so staff do not need extra steps between work and their own parish life. Do not require a separate personal-home/work-home switch. The role chooser in S03.01 selects the acting role; it does not introduce another layer of home selection.

**Refined answer:** The same dashboard contains the selected role's permitted responsibilities and the signed-in account's permitted personal/community information. Group related cards/sections clearly, using one navigation shell and shared account/language/appearance controls. Specific card priority remains for S03.07, which the owner has not answered.

One combined home does not combine every role's powers or reveal colleagues' personal information. It includes only information the current account may see. A secretary's own requests, personal notes or concerns, if available under their legitimate account/member permissions, remain account-private rather than becoming office/team records. No staff title automatically creates parish membership. The earlier blanket secretary personal-route restriction must be reviewed against this combined-home direction; exact personal-feature eligibility remains a permission-matrix detail rather than an assumed approval of every personal module.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Staff and permitted personal content share one combined home without exposing personal content to office colleagues.

### S03.03

**Question:** Which sections should appear in each role's main navigation, and which should be reachable only from a related record or a More menu?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:54](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:54). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Show sections according to permissions granted through roles and any authorized person-specific grants.

**Refined answer:** Use one navigation shell that reflects the selected role, current permitted parish/diocesan scope and any valid scoped individual grant. A role in one church must not reveal a section's records in a church where that permission is absent. View-only access shows viewing tools; edit/approval/release/export actions each require their relevant permission. Changing the visible menu does not itself grant or remove backend authority.

**Proposed organization:** Put frequent work at the top and group supporting modules under descriptive labels. The table below is a candidate arrangement of permission-enabled sections, not an approved fixed menu or a collection of separate home screens.

All retained modules must have an understandable destination for roles allowed to use them. A shorter primary navigation is not removal from scope. Show only authorized destinations; account/workspace controls remain available without any selected parish.

| Workspace | Primary destinations | Supporting grouped destinations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| System administration | Home, Organizations, Accounts & access, Administrative activity | Platform settings, scoped support/recovery and authorized system reports |
| Diocese/bishop | Home, Parishes, Appointments, My work, Diocese calendar | Authorized reports/finance, diocesan administration and relevant certificate-review queue if retained |
| Diocese administration | Home, Parishes, Accounts & access, My work | Scoped office support, reports, public information and explicitly delegated appointments |
| Priest | Home, Requests, Calendar, Reservations, Ministries, People | Households; sacramental preparation/records; Services & Activities; events/registrations/check-in; volunteers; facilities/equipment; communications/music; finance/office expenses; private pastoral work; reports/forms/audit/settings/administration as authorized |
| Parish Office — Parish Admin | Home, Requests, Calendar, Reservations, Ministries, People | Households, preparation, event forms/registrations/check-in, facilities/volunteers, permitted office expenses, public-content administration, permitted staff/settings/report tools |
| Parish Office — Secretary | Home, Requests, Calendar, Reservations, Ministries | People/households, sacramental preparation, Services & Activities, event forms/registrations/check-in, volunteers, facilities and Office Expenses; contextual in-app communication |
| Finance — Treasurer | Home, Giving, Finance, Reports | Permitted donor/household lookup, reconciliation, receipts, financial settings and authorized exports |
| Finance viewer | Overview, Finance, Reports | Only permitted viewing/printing/export; no editing routes |
| Ministry leader | Home, My ministries, Meetings/attendance, Volunteers, Calendar | Membership applications, resources/formation, ministry communication, services/music/check-in where explicitly assigned |
| Personal | Home, My requests, Ministries, Calendar, Inbox | Meetings, attendance, commitments, announcements/resources/formation, private notes, profile/official records, concerns, notifications and My account |

Exact labels/group placement should be validated in prototypes with the first two parishes; feature permissions remain controlled separately. Bishop review is included conditionally because its final policy remains open in S14.

Open person, household, request, certificate, event, reservation and ministry detail pages through their parent collections and related links. Keep editing, document release and individual history contextual to their record. Put infrequent account/settings controls in the account or relevant administrative menu. Do not put private cases in a broad More menu accessible to unrelated users.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Every authorized retained module has a destination; hiding a menu never substitutes for action checks.

### S03.04

**Question:** Which labels need changing to match users' language: People/Parishioners, Groups/Ministries, Member portal/Website content, Eparchy/Archdiocese, Services & Activities, or others?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:81](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:81). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner response:** “All of them.” Record this as a direction to review and standardize all the ambiguous labels listed in the question. It does not select the final English/French/Arabic wording of every replacement.

**Proposed completion:** Adopt an English/French/Arabic terminology dictionary. The labels below are proposed English labels; translated ecclesiastical terms and official organization names require approved language review rather than automatic transliteration.

| Current ambiguity | Proposed user-facing treatment |
| --- | --- |
| People / Parishioners | **People** for the office collection, since it can include visitors, children, clergy and other recorded persons; parish membership is a separate status |
| Groups / Ministries | **Ministries & Groups** for the collection; each record has a type such as choir, catechism class or committee |
| Dashboard / Home | One combined **Home** with the selected acting role and clear parish/combined-view context |
| My parish life / member Home | Personal/community content within the combined home and permitted direct destinations; no extra personal-home switch |
| Member portal / Website content | Public header: **Sign in** or **My account**; inside administration: **Public website → Content**, rather than calling the content editor Member portal |
| My account / My profile / My parish records | **My account** for login, preferences and appointments; personal profile content under it; **My parish records** for office-held facts and correction requests |
| Eparchy / Diocese / Archdiocese | Use the organization's approved ecclesiastical term in that context; internal generic labels must not overwrite its official identity |
| Requests / Forms | **Requests** for submitted work; **Event registrations** for event applications; **Forms & workflows** for reusable form/process definitions |
| Messages / Messaging / Notices | **Inbox** for private conversations; **Communications** for authorized audience composing/publishing; **Announcements** for published updates |
| Sacraments / Certificate | Use explicit labels: **Sacramental preparation**, **Official entry**, **Certificate request** and **Issued certificate**, according to the record/stage |
| Approval on behalf | **Record priest's approval**, with priest and actual entering secretary preserved in history |

Labels must describe actual outcomes. Do not call a submission a reservation confirmation, preparation an official record, an uploaded file a verified original, or a signed certificate ready for collection before all required later gates are satisfied.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Terminology dictionary disambiguates People, ministries, official records, account and public content in three languages.

### S03.05

**Question:** What should the parish selector show: assigned parishes, followed parishes, all accessible parishes, primary parish and/or a combined view?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:103](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:103). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** Use a **combined parish view**.

**Refined answer:** The combined home can show permitted information across the parishes associated with the account. Provide **All my parishes** and an optional parish filter rather than requiring repeated parish switches simply to browse activity. Each card, event, request and task identifies its parish and, where relevant, the role/authority through which it is visible.

Distinguish **Member**, **Following**, **Membership pending**, **Primary parish** and actual staff appointments. A followed parish contributes its published public information; an approved membership contributes permitted personal/member information; an active staff appointment contributes operational information only where the selected role/grant permits it. Primary parish is a personal default, not wider authority.

Combined display does not merge records or authority across parishes. When creating a request, event, reservation or other record, choose/confirm one target parish. When acting on an existing record, its own parish remains the target. If a different acting role is needed, offer an explicit role change rather than invisibly borrowing permission from another appointment.

Diocese/system scopes remain clearly labeled. A national directory or combined overview does not make every listed parish operationally editable. Similar parish names are disambiguated by locality/diocese. Detailed filter memory and default combined-view presentation remain UX refinements for validation.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Combined view labels each parish/relationship and every mutation retains one authorized parish target.

### S03.06

**Question:** What should persist after switching parish or workspace: current page, filters, selected date, open draft and last-used view? What must reset?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Recorded owner direction plus proposed detail. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:115](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:115). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner direction:** When a person's role changes, they must lose the information/actions their previous role no longer authorizes. An open page or remembered view does not preserve the former access.

**Refined answer:** Refresh the available role choices, navigation, combined dashboard, search results, counts and record/action permissions when appointments change. Apply the new authority to protected reads and writes without waiting for a new login. Remove now-inaccessible detail content from active views; previously delivered information cannot be assumed to have been unseen. If the selected role is no longer available, show the updated role choice or an allowed home/pending state. Unrelated valid roles/parish relationships remain intact.

**Proposed completion of the remaining view-memory question:** Remember language, appearance, accessibility preferences and collapsed navigation per account. Remember collection view, allowed columns, sort, page size, filters and calendar position separately for each account/role/parish where appropriate, including the combined-view filter.

When switching role within the same parish, retain a compatible calendar period or collection filter only if its fields and records remain permitted. When switching parish, restore that parish's own last view or use a safe default. Never carry a person ID, selected row, pending approval, resource, household or document into another parish.

The current page may stay open only when its collection exists and is authorized in the destination. Otherwise return to the combined home or an appropriate allowed/pending state and explain the change. Preserve recovery material only where the user remains entitled to retain it.

For unsaved changes, offer **Save draft**, **Discard** or **Stay here**, only where a draft is supported and the account may retain it. Submitted facts cannot be moved to another parish by changing the selector. Clear bulk selections, close approval/release confirmations and recheck authority before any subsequent action.

Each open tab maintains its own target context. Another tab's parish switch must not silently change the target of an existing form. Remembered settings are preferences, not permission grants; validate them after a role is removed or a module becomes unavailable.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Preferences remain scoped; switching clears unsafe selections and revoked grants remove stale records/counts.

### S03.07

**Question:** For each dashboard, choose the information and actions that deserve the first visible screen. Which numbers need definitions, date periods and drill-down destinations?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:131](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:131). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Owner answer: Open.** The owner left item 7 blank. The dashboard layout, cards, priorities and metrics below remain recommendations, adapted to one combined home; they have not been approved by the blank response.

The first visible area should show the active context, today's relevant responsibilities, work the user can actually act on, and useful next actions. Calendar, reservations and ministries get prominent placement in parish workspaces, consistent with S01 priorities.

| Workspace | First-screen priorities |
| --- | --- |
| Priest | Needs my decision; today's/upcoming calendar; reservations requiring his decision; ministry/office exceptions; **Recorded on my behalf** activity; quick links to Requests/Calendar |
| Secretary/Parish Office | Today's calendar; preparation/follow-up queue; reservations awaiting office work; event-form/registration issues; ministry coordination; Create request/event/reservation where permitted |
| Bishop | Diocesan work requiring his authority; parish/appointment exceptions; upcoming diocesan responsibilities; scoped overview with explicit date period; conditional certificate decisions |
| Diocese administrator | Onboarding/appointment tasks, authorized parish support, pending requests in own scope and administrative follow-up |
| Super Admin | Initialization where applicable; organization/account administration; actual support/access issues; platform status only from real available information |
| Treasurer | Open finance tasks, actual count/reconciliation work, authorized approvals, dated balances separated by currency and pending evidence |
| Finance viewer | Scoped financial summaries/reports with date range and no transaction-entry controls |
| Ministry leader | Next meetings, pending permitted membership work, attendance not yet recorded, volunteer gaps and tasks for assigned ministries |
| Personal | Own active requests and next steps, upcoming permitted activities/commitments, unread messages/notifications and membership/onboarding progress |

Every metric defines **record unit, organization scope, period, applicable statuses, refresh time and drill-down**. Examples:

- **Needs my decision:** Distinct authorized open cases whose next available decision belongs to this acting capacity. Excludes information-only updates and cases blocked by unmet prerequisites.
- **Office preparation:** Distinct open cases awaiting a required office step; show whether assigned to me, another colleague or unassigned office work.
- **Upcoming reservations:** Confirmed reservations in the displayed upcoming period, with tentative requests shown separately.
- **Ministry members:** Active roster membership in the selected group/scope; “memberships” and unique people must not be conflated across several groups.
- **Unread messages:** Conversations/messages addressed to the current account according to one consistently defined read unit; not staff-wide message volume.

Show missing/unrecorded data as **Not recorded**, **No data for this period** or **Unavailable**, rather than fabricated sample values or an unjustified zero. Confidential case counts are absent for unauthorized users. **Recorded on my behalf** is an activity/notification item, not an approval still waiting for the priest to repeat it.

**Reviewed completion:** The recommended first-screen cards are a completion of your blank item, not an inferred approval. Quantities and filters resolve through MT01–MT15 in document-and-report-specifications.md; initial slots are My action, Today/upcoming, Reservations, Ministries and actual recorded-on-my-behalf activity for priest. Keep optional personal activity below the role-critical work in the same Home.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Each role’s first-screen cards link to real work and each displayed number has a defined period/unit.

### S03.08

**Question:** Should actionable work appear in one personal queue across request types, or in separate role/module queues? Distinguish “needs me,” “needs office,” and “waiting on applicant.”

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:159](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:159). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Provide **My work** as a unified triage experience across the user's current authorized scope, with clear filters rather than merging underlying record types into one undifferentiated process.

Primary views should be **Needs my action**, **Office/team work**, **Waiting**, **Completed** and **All permitted**. Waiting can be filtered to applicant information/documents, another authority, planned date or an external dependency. Group/filter by parish, type, stage, owner, due date and priority where those facts exist.

Requests remains the principal intake/processing collection. Membership, profile corrections, guests, sacramental requests, bookings and event-related work can appear in the same triage interface while opening their specific review screens. Existing module queues remain useful filtered views of the same canonical work, not competing copies with different status/count rules.

Each row shows reference, subject, parish, request type, current stage, next action, responsible person/role and relevant received/due/last-updated date. Internal notes and applicant-visible replies remain separate.

An optional **Across my workspaces** overview may aggregate authorized work for one account. Actions require the correct acting workspace; selecting an item offers an explicit context switch. It does not combine powers from unrelated assignments. Confidential concerns, private pastoral work and restricted incidents use separate authorized queues and do not leak titles, existence or counts through the general inbox.

Accepted online/guest work that links to an office record retains its origin/reference without appearing twice for the same next step. A secretary can record an already-given priest instruction through the case's authorized action even though the normal digital decision queue points to the priest; the interface must not demand a nonexistent prior online instruction.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** My work distinguishes needs-me, team work and waiting without duplicate linked intake/office cases.

### S03.09

**Question:** What exactly should each navigation badge count? Resolve whether it includes guest requests, membership, corrections, waitlists, bishop review and work someone else must perform.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:173](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:173). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Navigation badges indicate **authorized outstanding work**, not the total size of a collection. Put collection totals such as People/Households/Ministries inside their pages, where their meaning is clearer. Put unread counts on Inbox/Notifications separately.

Recommended rules:

1. Define one canonical actionable case per workflow record with a currently permitted next action. A linked online submission and resulting office record do not count as two cases for the same work.
2. **Requests** counts actionable cases in the selected workspace/scope, including membership, corrections and guest work where that user can act. Show their category breakdown inside the queue.
3. A combined **My work** total is a deduplicated union, not the arithmetic sum of several overlapping module badges.
4. Waitlists contribute the number of event waitlists requiring a staff decision if rows represent events; participant counts are separately labeled. Never mix “events needing review” with “people waiting” under one unexplained number.
5. Priest/bishop decisions count only when the user has the relevant decision and actual stage is ready. Unresolved bishop policy does not create an automatic bishop badge.
6. Information-only recorded-priest-approval updates count as unread activity/notifications where relevant, not as approvals waiting again.
7. Exclude closed, withdrawn, cancelled, finished and inaccessible cases. Work assigned to another person appears in an authorized team view rather than inflating **Needs me**.
8. All badge/list/dashboard figures use the same scope and unit. A filter clearly explains why a visible subset differs from the unfiltered badge. Show loading/failure instead of treating an unknown count as zero.

After transitions or access changes, refresh counts and lists consistently. No count, tooltip, search result, exported total or cross-parish summary may reveal a restricted concern's existence to an unassigned user.

**Reviewed completion:** Badge definitions are MT01–MT03. Unread Inbox counts messages, not conversations; notifications count their own unread notice IDs. Waitlist operational badge counts event waitlists needing a decision and labels participant count separately. Server result unknown/error never becomes zero.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Badge and filtered queue use the same deduplicated case unit and exclude inaccessible confidential cases.

### S03.10

**Question:** What should global search find for each role, and which fields may results expose? Include names in either script, phone, household, request reference, register number and pages/actions.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:190](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:190). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Search should find permitted records and destinations using English, French and Arabic names/content, supplied alternate official names, phone, request reference, register number, household and allowed event/ministry/resource fields. Preserve stored names; searching should not rewrite official spellings or invent translations.

Default staff search to the active parish/workspace. Offer an explicit wider scope only when authorized. Public search searches only published public information. Personal search searches the person's permitted requests, conversations and community records rather than the staff directory. System account administration has a separate authorized account lookup, not a public identity search.

Group results by type and identify parish/locality, record label, reference and permitted status. Match sensitivity must be respected before returning results or counts. Do not expose donor details, medical data, internal notes, document contents or private account identities merely because they match text.

Confidential concerns, pastoral/private notes and private conversations should use their dedicated permitted search surfaces. Global search may offer the destination **My concerns** or **My notes** without indexing other people's content. No search suggestion should confirm the existence of a restricted case.

Phone/email search must account for permitted normalization/international formats while preserving original data. Searching a number does not authorize its public disclosure. If nothing matches, offer a permitted next action such as changing search scope or creating a new record after duplicate checking; do not automatically create one.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Search returns only permitted fields/records across supplied scripts, never private-note/concern leakage.

### S03.11

**Question:** What should selecting a search result open: a page, drawer or relevant tab? How should users return to the same result position and filters?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:202](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:202). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Selecting a result should open the stable detail page for that record and relevant tab. Use full pages for requests/timelines, people/households, event/reservation details, ministry records and official-entry/certificate work. Drawers serve short edits or previews without replacing the only addressable version of a record.

If the result belongs to another permitted parish/workspace, name the destination and offer an explicit switch. Preserve the search query, allowed scope, filters, sort, pagination and scroll position for **Back to results**. Breadcrumbs should explain the record's parent collection rather than force a browser-history guess.

Recheck access and record state when opening and again before action. If the result is now archived, show an authorized archive detail with a status banner. If it is no longer available, explain the limited situation and offer a safe return without exposing a prior confidential title. A notification, bookmark and search result should resolve to the same underlying record rather than three competing copies.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.
