**Acceptance:** Result opens stable relevant detail and Back restores authorized query, filter, page and position.

### S03.12

**Question:** Which tables need saved filters, sort, column choices, page-size choices, bulk actions and selected-versus-all-matching selection?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:210](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:210). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Support consistent search/filter/sort/pagination on People, Households, Requests, Ministries, Registrations, Reservations, Facilities/Equipment, financial collections, reports, and authorized account/administrative history lists.

Save preferences per account and relevant parish/workspace. Provide useful defaults, visible active filters and **Reset view**. Proposed page-size choices are 10, 25, 50 and 100 where appropriate; large administrative collections should not attempt an unbounded “show everything” screen. Restricted fields cannot be added through a column picker.

Selection must distinguish **Select this page** from **Select all matching [count]**. A selected-count summary persists while selections exist. Changing scope/filter must clear selection or explicitly explain which selected records remain; no hidden selection may be acted upon accidentally.

Allow bulk actions only when each record is eligible and the action is understandable: permitted export, reminders through working channels, assignment or eligible archive. Before mutation/export, show record count, scope, action and any excluded/ineligible items. Return item-level outcomes and preserve successful results when some items fail.

Do not introduce blanket bulk sacramental signing, signature application, guest-file release, sensitive-case action or independent financial approval as a convenience. Those require separate explicit workflow authorization. Bulk recording of a priest's offline instruction, if ever permitted, must enumerate the cases and preserve per-case attribution; it is not approved by this section. Export scope is explicit: **Selected**, **All matching filters**, or an authorized complete collection.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Select-page and select-all-matching/export outcomes are explicit with item-level partial failures.

### S03.13

**Question:** On a phone, which actions and fields must remain immediately visible when desktop tables become cards or hide columns? Which tasks need a dedicated full-screen flow?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:222](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:222). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Although laptops are primary, phone layouts must support public/member journeys and essential away-from-office staff work. Transform long rows into cards or labeled detail expansions when needed. Horizontal scrolling is acceptable for genuinely two-dimensional calendars/matrices, with an obvious indication and an accessible list/detail alternative.

Each actionable request/reservation card retains its reference/type, subject, parish, stage, next action, relevant date and responsible role. A money card retains actual currency/amount and status; guardian/medical fields remain restricted rather than casually copied onto a public-facing card.

Use full-screen flows for long requests, complex person/household editing, reservation selection, document review/release and consequential approval confirmations. Keep the current parish, acting role, authorizing priest where applicable, primary action, Back/Cancel and visible validation. Prevent keyboards or fixed bottom navigation from covering errors and final controls.

Offer touch/keyboard alternatives to drag-and-drop, hover menus and tiny calendar cells. A tap to open detail must not also approve. Do not conceal an essential status or action solely to make the layout fit. Camera/file upload and return-from-reauthentication must preserve the permitted draft context.

**Acceptance:** Phone cards retain parish/reference/state/next actor/date and currency while complex actions remain usable.

### S03.14

**Question:** When a direct link points to a moved, archived, removed or unauthorized record, what should the user see and where should they be able to go next?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:232](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:232). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Use a consistent access-checked record resolution experience:

- **Moved/renamed record:** Redirect only to its verified successor within the user's authority, preserving context and a simple explanatory notice. Do not infer a match from a similar name.
- **Archived record:** Show a read-only detail/status when permitted, with restoration only for authorized roles. Archiving should not automatically break all historical links.
- **Closed/cancelled workflow:** Retain its history and outcome; show any permitted next request/reopening action rather than a live approval control.
- **Unauthenticated user:** Sign in, then return after checking access. Do not expose the record title/content on the login page.
- **No longer authorized or record unavailable:** Use a neutral **This item is unavailable or you do not have access** response without confirming private record existence. Offer Back, workspace Home or a nonrevealing access/support route.
- **Expired/revoked guest tracking link:** Offer the office's approved recovery/contact process without revealing another applicant's request or issuing a new link merely from a claimed name.

Detailed distinctions can be shown only to authorized administrators/support staff. Error pages must not contain previous confidential titles, amounts or identities. A permanently removed unused setup is different from an archived institutional record and must not turn into a public list of former private contents.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; representative role users; head priests. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF52](workflow-specifications.md#wf52), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s03). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A27](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a27), [A28](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a28).

**Acceptance:** Unavailable/unauthorized links reveal no private existence and offer safe navigation or reviewed recovery.

## S04 — Public directory, parish pages and visitor discovery

### S04.01

**Question:** What is the public homepage's main job: finding a parish, finding Mass times, making a request, or explaining ParishLife? Rank the primary actions.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:247](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:247). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

The public homepage is primarily a useful parish-discovery and visiting tool. Proposed priority:

1. **Find a parish** by name, place or diocese.
2. **Find Mass/confession times** and plan a visit.
3. **Contact or make a request to the correct parish**.
4. Discover public activities and ministries.
5. Learn about ParishLife and adoption by parish teams.

The first screen should provide an obvious search/Find a parish action, language control and Sign in/My account. Place Mass-time search within easy reach. Keep introductory imagery/copy concise enough that it does not bury these tasks, especially on phones.

For a returning visitor, offer their previously selected parish without redirecting them away from the directory automatically. A generic homepage must not silently select the first parish in the database. Once a visitor chooses a parish, request/contact actions clearly identify that parish before submission.

The directory represents participating/published parishes, not an asserted complete list of every church in Lebanon. At initial launch it may legitimately show only the two participating parishes. The interface should scale to additional dioceses without fabricated sample parishes, visits, events or live activity counters.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Homepage action order prioritizes parish discovery, published times and correct-parish contact before marketing.

### S04.02

**Question:** Which directory filters and sort choices are essential, and should visitors find Masses by day, time and language across parishes rather than only opening parish profiles?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:263](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:263). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Provide text search across approved English/French/Arabic parish names and locality names. Useful directory filters are diocese, locality/region, supported rite/jurisdiction where relevant, and **Online requests available**. At national scale, reveal hierarchical location filters progressively; do not force several geographic selections before a visitor can search by name.

Default sort is parish name in the chosen display language, with locality and optional nearest-distance alternatives. Always show locality/diocese to disambiguate similar church names. Do not introduce an unexplained recommendation ranking or make the nearest parish look like the visitor's automatically assigned parish.

Offer a separate **Find a Mass** search across published participating parishes, with date/day, time range, celebration language, parish/locality/diocese and service type where supported. Confession availability should be clearly distinguished from Mass; appointment-only confession appears as such, not as an invented timed session.

Results require structured recurring schedules with actual dated exceptions/cancellations so “next Mass” and time filters have defensible meanings. This is a design dependency for S05.08/S16; existing free-text times must not be parsed or guessed into supposedly verified occurrences. Where structured data is unavailable, show the parish's approved published schedule text and a contact action, with exact-date filtering unavailable for that record.

Give **Today**, a chosen date and a clearly defined upcoming period, displaying parish-local date/time and celebration language. Surface published changes/cancellations and avoid claiming real-time confirmation when the parish only maintains a posted schedule.

Show the results count, active filters, Clear filters and helpful no-result alternatives. Never translate “no schedule published” into “no services exist.”

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Time search uses actual structured occurrences/exceptions; absent schedule is not no services.

### S04.03

**Question:** Which details must a parish card show before a visitor opens it, including office availability or whether online requests are accepted?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:277](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:277). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Each directory card should identify the parish and help a visitor decide whether to open it without exposing internal records.

Required card information:

- Approved parish name in the selected language, with other supplied official names accessible when useful.
- Locality and diocese; relevant rite/jurisdiction label only when accurate and helpful.
- Verified parish photo or neutral church illustration/emblem.
- Clear **View parish** action; a separate useful contact/request action where genuinely available.

Optional, only when supported by actual published information:

- Next published Mass time/language from the dated schedule.
- **Online requests available** or **Contact parish office**.
- Published office hours; **Open now** only when structured hours, parish time zone and exceptions support the calculation.
- Approximate distance when location/coordinates are valid.
- Verified accessibility information, avoiding ambiguous unsupported “accessible” claims.

Missing data should not be replaced with guessed times, personal numbers or sample photographs presented as actual parish images. “Hours not published” is different from “Office closed.” Deactivated/closed parishes must not receive an active request button; any retained public historical listing clearly identifies status and the appropriate contact/custodian.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Cards disambiguate locality/diocese and show only genuinely published contact/time/distance claims.

### S04.04

**Question:** Is the map preview useful at launch, or should it be hidden until a live map is available? What must happen when location access is refused or coordinates are missing?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:298](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:298). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Hide the nonfunctional map preview from ordinary public navigation until a working geographic map is configured. Retain real-map support in the product scope; an unconfigured integration is an availability state rather than a reason to remove the feature permanently. The directory/list and verified directions links remain fully useful without it.

A future map must reflect the same published parishes and filters as the list, use verified locations and offer a list alternative. It cannot display fabricated pins or suggest that an inaccurate illustrative location is verified.

Request browser location only after the visitor selects **Use my location**. Explain its purpose as nearby sorting/filtering. If refused, unavailable or inaccurate, preserve the ordinary directory and let the visitor enter a town/region; do not repeatedly prompt or require permission to browse.

When distance is enabled, label it approximate. Selecting a radius should genuinely limit results with known coordinates to that radius; offer an explicitly labeled way to view more. Parishes without coordinates may appear in a separate **Distance unavailable** group or ordinary name/locality results, not as if they met the radius. Do not calculate directions from a parish name when a verified address/coordinate is required to identify the correct church.

Keep precise visitor coordinates out of shared URLs and ordinary logs/exports. Propose session-only nearby preferences with a clear **Clear location** control. External map/directions navigation should name the destination/provider and use only approved public parish location information.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Denied location/unconfigured map leaves manual directory usable and never invents coordinates or pins.

### S04.05

**Question:** What must every parish profile contain, and in what order should story, visiting information, times, clergy, ministries, events, requests, updates and contacts appear?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:310](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:310). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Use one consistent public profile structure across participating dioceses, populated with approved parish information rather than staff-state data. The proposed order prioritizes visiting and contact:

1. **Identity and actions:** Parish name, locality/diocese, verified image/emblem and clear status; View times, Make a request, Contact and Directions as available.
2. **Mass/confession times:** Published schedules, celebration languages and specific exceptions/cancellations; avoid hiding this practical information below a long parish story.
3. **Plan your visit:** Verified address/directions, office contact/hours and accurate accessibility information.
4. **Parish calendar:** Upcoming published activities with a dedicated full-calendar link and explicit public details.
5. **Requests and parish services:** Relevant request types with a plain-language explanation that office/priest review follows submission.
6. **Ministries & groups:** Approved description, eligibility/schedule where public and Ask about joining/Apply through the appropriate route.
7. **Meet the parish:** Approved clergy names/titles/roles; approved ministry contact roles, using office contact defaults.
8. **Latest announcements:** Current published notices with dates and expiry where relevant.
9. **About/history and gallery:** Verified story, supplied imagery/captions and descriptive text.
10. **Contact footer:** Office details, maintained contact hours, other official links and the relevant next action.

Use a simple section navigation/contents menu and shareable public event/request pages. Hide optional empty sections cleanly without breaking navigation. Keep Request/Contact reachable on phones without intrusive controls covering content. Private family names, attendance, request status, finances or personal profiles never appear merely because they are linked to a public event or ministry.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Parish profile order supports visiting, contact and requests before optional history/gallery.

### S04.06

**Question:** Should missing parish information be hidden, shown as awaiting publication, or replaced with a specific contact action? Which missing fields should prevent publication?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:327](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:327). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Distinguish **required identity/readiness**, **useful but unpublished** and **optional content**.

Minimum proposed public/operational activation requirements: correct organization identity, approved English/French/Arabic core parish labels, verified diocese/locality, an active responsible priest/authorized contact owner, adoption/activation approval and at least one usable public office contact route or explicitly staffed contact mechanism. Publish a verified address/location or accurately indicate its absence; do not invent coordinates.

These readiness checks must be compatible with S02.03's **Create and activate** action. Once required setup is confirmed, creation activates/publicizes the parish without an additional unpublished queue. Incomplete setup can remain a private draft. The owner must approve any change to what counts as minimum readiness before implementation.

For missing useful information, show a limited honest prompt such as **Mass times have not been published. Contact the parish office to confirm.** An unpublished confession schedule or office hours should not be shown as closed/unavailable in fact. Hide optional story, empty gallery or ministries without public descriptions; absence of a gallery must not prevent an otherwise ready parish from operating.

Core public labels and reusable content follow the proposed three-language publication policy. Editors see missing-language readiness before publishing. Partial optional content can remain draft while the existing complete public page stays available. A content fallback must be explicit and must not disguise incomplete French/Arabic support as completed translation.

Wrong identity/diocese, no authorized responsible office, inaccurate mandatory contact or an unapproved parish must block activation, not merely display a decorative warning. Exact jurisdiction and names remain owner/diocese inputs; this draft does not fill them from sample data.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Minimum correct core setup aligns with immediate valid activation; optional empty sections never block it.

### S04.07

**Question:** Should illustrative photographs remain on named parish pages until verified parish images exist? Approve the wording and placement of the illustration label.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:341](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:341). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Prefer verified images supplied/approved by the parish. Until available, use a neutral church emblem or clearly illustrative nonidentifying artwork on named parish cards/pages rather than an unrelated real church photograph suggesting it depicts that parish.

General homepage imagery may remain illustrative when labeled near its use and appropriately attributed. Proposed wording is **Illustrative image — not a photograph of this parish.** A footer credit alone is insufficient if a named parish's hero visually implies an authentic local photograph.

Record image source, approval, caption and descriptive text in the content workflow. Photos of identifiable people, particularly children, require the parish's approved publication procedure; uploading an image is not itself permission to publish it. Inspect captions/alt text for private names or details before publication.

When a real image is withdrawn or unavailable, return to the neutral fallback and retain layout/readability. Do not require uploading photographs to activate the parish. French/Arabic image descriptions and labels are part of launch content readiness.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Named parish pages use verified photos or neutral/labeled illustration, never unrelated authentic-looking church image.

### S04.08

**Question:** Which clergy/leader names and contact details may be public, and who confirms their publication? Should contact always route through the parish office?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:351](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:351). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Publish only approved public clergy information: supplied name, ecclesiastical title, parish function/head designation and relevant official parish contact. Staff/clergy appointment changes should trigger review of the public listing; an internal person record is not automatically a public profile.

Ministry pages may show an approved leader name or role where the parish and relevant person have authorized publication. Default contact is the parish/ministry office route rather than the leader's personal phone/email. A person may supply a genuinely intended public contact, but it must be explicitly designated and removable; never copy an account's login contact into a website field automatically.

The head priest is accountable for parish public-contact correctness; appointed office staff may prepare/maintain it under the agreed publishing authority. Diocese/bishop authority validates clergy title and appointment facts. Public publishing permission and clergy appointment permission are separate.

Contact actions should clearly show which office receives the message, available hours and whether the route is phone, email, external service or in-system request. Do not imply an external channel delivers when it is only a stored preference. Where a leader leaves or a number changes, update the public contact and offer a maintained office fallback without revealing the former contact's private record.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Public clergy/leader names and contact destinations have actual publication approval; login contacts stay private.

### S04.09

**Question:** Should public calendar titles include family names for baptisms, weddings and funerals? Define default visibility and who authorizes exceptions.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:361](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:361). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Default publicly visible sacramental events to generic titles such as **Baptism celebration**, **Wedding celebration** or **Funeral service**, with the approved time/location. Do not automatically reuse the internal request title, household surname or person name as public calendar text.

Provide separate fields for internal title/details and approved public title/description. Visibility also applies to linked images, captions, attendee lists, documents, calendar feeds/downloads, search snippets, reminder content and shared previews; a public event is not permission to publish all its related records.

A named public announcement/event may be allowed only through the parish's explicit publication procedure, with the relevant subject/authorized family approval and authorized parish publication approval. Staff should record the approval scope rather than assuming that requesting the sacrament means agreeing to public publicity. Minor/guardian and funeral-announcement handling must follow the final parish/diocesan policy specified in later sections.

If publicity is withdrawn or corrected, update future public displays/feeds and keep an appropriate internal history. The system cannot honestly promise to retract copies already downloaded/shared. Staff/member/clergy audiences may receive different details only where the corresponding access rules permit them; public names cannot be restored through an alternate export or list view.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Internal sacramental family names do not appear in public titles/feeds without separate naming permission.

### S04.10

**Question:** Which guest request types should be discoverable from parish pages? The public form also contains appointment and ministry options beyond the main request cards.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:371](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:371). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Offer clear request groups on the parish page, with only configured, genuinely supported choices active:

| Group | Discoverable request types and expectations |
| --- | --- |
| Sacraments and official documents | Baptism, First Communion, confirmation/chrismation, marriage, funeral and certificate, according to approved parish/jurisdiction support |
| Facilities | Hall/room/outdoor-space booking where supported; show permitted availability without other applicants' private details |
| Pastoral services | House blessing, sick/home visit, Mass intention, meeting/appointment with priest and another pastoral request |
| Parish/community | Ministry inquiry and other general office requests |

An inquiry about joining a ministry is not approval of ministry membership. A guest appointment request is not an automatically reserved time. A booking request is not confirmed occupancy. A certificate request is not issuance. Every type must state who handles it and the next expected step.

Guest and member versions should collect the same essential facts for the service, using conditional structured questions where necessary. Signed-in linked members can prefill permitted household/person data; guests provide their own information with only the necessary contact and relationship details. Exact fields, authorization for others and supporting documents remain S11–S15 decisions. Do not demand an account merely to contact or make a supported guest request.

Before submission, show selected parish, request type, subject, supplied details, contact method, required physical follow-up and an understandable review summary. Submitting a sacramental need routes it to authorized preparation and priest decisions, including the already-agreed secretary-recorded-priest-instruction path when applicable; it does not give a guest internal sacramental access.

After submission, show a reference and private tracking route with clear instructions to keep it safe. Permit the future office-reviewed association to an account; do not auto-create membership/person/staff access from a guest submission. Tracking tokens and private document URLs must never appear in public search, share buttons or event previews.

When online requests are disabled for the parish or a particular type, show **Contact the parish office** with the real route and relevant hours. Existing applicants retain the authorized tracking/follow-up route even when new submissions close. Public ministry inquiries and signed-in formal ministry applications remain clearly distinguished.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Supported guest request types state their true next step; inquiry/submission never implies approval or booking.

### S04.11

**Question:** Should urgent needs such as a funeral or sick visit offer a clearly visible office/emergency contact route alongside online submission? Who maintains that contact and its availability?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:392](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:392). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Provide an obvious **Urgent pastoral need? Contact the parish** route for funeral arrangements, a sick visit or another time-sensitive pastoral matter. Use a direct, maintained office/designated pastoral contact where supplied. An online request can accompany the contact but must not imply immediate review.

Display contact hours and any actually maintained out-of-hours number. **24-hour** or **emergency** availability is used only when the parish has designated a real staffed arrangement. ParishLife's online queue is not automatically an emergency dispatch or continuously monitored response service.

The head priest is accountable for this route; authorized office staff keep details and exceptions current. Require periodic confirmation when parish leadership/contact arrangements change. If no out-of-hours route exists, state the published availability plainly instead of inventing one or repeatedly suggesting that an unavailable office is staffed.

Messages must distinguish **request received** from **someone has read/responded**. Do not promise SMS/email/WhatsApp alerts until those services actually deliver. Urgency may flag permitted office/priest work, but it does not bypass confidential access, identity review, priest authority or official document requirements.

Specific contact numbers/hours and escalation arrangements must be supplied by each parish. None are guessed from church names or current sample records.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Urgent contact shows actual maintained hours/route and never promises continuous online response.

### S04.12

**Question:** What should shareable parish/event URLs, visitor language choice and return-to-results behavior preserve? Should the separate landing/marketing page remain part of the product?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:404](/C:/Users/User/Desktop/S03-S04-proposed-answers.md:404). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

Give every published parish and public event a stable, shareable public URL. Resolve by an unambiguous stable identity, with readable names where useful; similar names in different towns must never collide. Renaming a parish should preserve an access-checked redirect from its old public link.

Preserve appropriate public directory state in links/history: text query, locality/diocese filters, sort, selected date/service filters, view and language. Preserve browser return position/pagination when going back from a profile. Precise visitor location, tracking tokens, private filters, account identities and confidential record references do not belong in public sharing URLs.

Keep the visitor's chosen English/French/Arabic language through directory, profile, event, request, success and contact journeys. A language switch retains the current parish and permitted form state. Public share previews must contain the approved public translation/title, not private internal event details. Missing optional translations follow the agreed publication policy without silently substituting incorrect official names.

Keep the current public directory/parish site as the public service entry point. Retain a separate marketing/about area for **About ParishLife / For parish teams**, reachable through appropriate navigation/footer links, with product explanation, bundles and adoption/contact information. Avoid two competing sites each pretending to be the parish directory or showing divergent parish information.

The marketing page must accurately describe configured product capabilities. It does not initiate billing merely because bundles appear. Public **Sign in** returns existing users to the relevant account/workspace, with **Create account** available without interrupting guest browsing. After login from a legitimate public request link, retain the intended parish/type while rechecking actual membership and authority.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product owners; parish public-content owner; head priest; language reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF51](workflow-specifications.md#wf51), [WF11](workflow-specifications.md#wf11); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s04).

**Acceptance:** Stable public URLs preserve safe language/filter state without tracking tokens or precise visitor coordinates.

## S05 — Website content, announcements and publishing

### S05.01

**Question:** Who may edit public content, who may publish it, and should clergy or another reviewer approve particular types before publication?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6609](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Parish Admins, secretaries and priests with content permission prepare public text/media within their parish. The head priest or an explicitly appointed public-content publisher approves ordinary publication; clergy titles, organizational facts and official sacramental wording require their competent authority. Leaders prepare material only for assigned ministries/audiences.

Keep edit and publish rights distinct, including urgent corrections. A colleague cannot approve their own content where a second review is configured. Every publication identifies editor, publisher, revision, language readiness and audience. Public access derives from approved publication, not from an internal record existing.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Editor and publisher permissions are separate and domain facts still require their competent authority.

### S05.02

**Question:** Should public profile details and website sections be managed together, or should their different ownership remain visible as separate editors?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6617](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Provide one Public website management area with Overview, Parish details, Schedules, Content, Announcements and Gallery. Each field retains its own authority: office editors maintain approved contact/visiting information, clergy/diocese control appointment/title facts, and content publishers control sections.

Show current public output, draft changes, all three language states and the action required. Avoid separate editors with contradictory copies of office hours, Mass times or contact information. Related administrative records can be linked read-only where this editor cannot change them. One area simplifies navigation without merging permissions or erasing responsibility.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** One website area uses authoritative contact/schedule sources without merging field ownership.

### S05.03

**Question:** When editing published content, should Save draft retain the currently published version? Confirm or replace the current behavior that unpublishes a section.

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6625](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Save draft keeps the current published revision online. New unpublished content remains private; editing a published section creates a separate draft. Unpublishing is an explicit action with audience/impact confirmation, reason and history.

A draft save must never remove a live section as a hidden side effect. Preview clearly labels the version being viewed. Publishing promotes one reviewed language-complete revision; concurrent public changes trigger comparison. If a publisher withdraws incorrect content, choose restore previous approved version or explicit unpublish, with maintained contact information and a visible result.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Saving a new draft leaves current approved public version online until explicit publication/unpublish.

### S05.04

**Question:** Which publishing states are needed: draft, awaiting approval, scheduled, published, expired, returned and archived? Who moves between them?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6633](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Use Draft, Awaiting review, Returned, Approved/Scheduled, Published, Expired/Unpublished and Archived. Editors submit; authorized reviewers return/approve; publishers publish/schedule/withdraw. Scheduler-backed transitions only run when the actual service exists; otherwise show a manual publishing task.

Record who changed state, reason where needed and actual effective time. Scheduled content displays parish time zone, audience and cancellation control. Expiry removes public distribution but retains authorized history. Archive is not permanent deletion. Existing published content remains online while a replacement is returned for edits; avoid ambiguous mixed draft/published labels.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Publication state changes name actual actor/time and scheduled execution is never claimed without runner.

### S05.05

**Question:** Is publishing allowed with only one language complete? If so, what should visitors and editors see when the other translation is missing?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6641](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Core public pages, reusable announcements/forms and official content require reviewed English/French/Arabic versions before final publication, consistent with launch language scope. Editors can save partial drafts; show missing/review-needed languages and the responsible reviewer.

Do not silently advertise a partially translated item as complete. The last approved trilingual version remains live. Private user free text retains its original language and does not require three authored copies; this remains the explicit interpretation to approve under S01.09. Any future urgent-language exception needs its own named authority/process and visible fallback, not an undocumented bypass.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Missing required translation blocks replacement publication while approved trilingual live content remains.

### S05.06

**Question:** Must editors preview the exact public page on phone and desktop before publishing, including language fallback and private/public visibility?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6649](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Require a preview of the actual pending public revision, with phone/desktop and EN/FR/AR controls. Show full page context, links, image descriptions, dates, schedule exceptions and public versus restricted audience. Label draft previews private and prevent public sharing/indexing of private previews.

Before publish, display changed sections, language readiness, recipient/audience scope and scheduled effective time. Preview must use the same rendering/content rules as publication. Review should catch long names, missing captions and wrong contact destinations. Preview alone does not grant publishing rights or mark documents officially approved.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Preview uses exact pending version/audience across phone/desktop and EN/FR/AR.

### S05.07

**Question:** Which content should support rich text, links, files, galleries and captions? Who provides image descriptions and confirms permission to use photographs of people?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6657](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Allow controlled rich text, safe links and approved images/files on stories, announcements, ministry descriptions and resources; structured schedule/contact fields remain structured. Avoid arbitrary embed/code entry for ordinary editors. Each image/file has title, description/caption, language, source, approval and intended audience.

The uploader supplies descriptive text and the publication-permission basis; the publisher verifies these before public use. Identify people only where approved. Private evidence and certificates are not reusable website media by default. Replacement/withdrawal retains authorized revision history and updates future public references. Rights and retention owners provide the applicable rules.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Media has source/rights/descriptions and private evidence cannot become public media automatically.

### S05.08

**Question:** Should Mass/confession/office times be structured schedules with exceptions or free text? Who keeps holiday changes consistent with the calendar?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6665](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Store Mass/confession/office schedules as structured recurrence rules with dates, times, language, location, time zone and dated exceptions; retain supplementary explanatory text such as By appointment. Authorized office users prepare changes and the priest/publisher confirms relevant public schedules.

One authoritative schedule feeds parish profiles, Find a Mass, calendars and card summaries. A dated cancellation/holiday exception overrides the recurring occurrence rather than creating contradictory listings. Imported free text remains text pending review, not automatically parsed into trusted occurrences. Show publication/update date and source, and notify affected registered participants where actual event changes require it.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Dated schedule exceptions override recurrence consistently in directory, calendar and profile.

### S05.09

**Question:** Do announcements need pinning, expiry, categories, audiences, attachments and scheduled publication? Which should appear on both public and member pages?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6673](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Announcements support audience, category, pinning, publish/expiry time, translations, attachments and an accountable author/publisher. Public/parish/member/group visibility is explicit; group updates do not automatically become public.

A single approved content identity may have permitted placements on the public website and combined home, preserving one revision/history. Audience changes require review and must not broaden access to formerly private attachments. Scheduled/expired behavior depends on a real runner; manual fallback is labeled. Keep historical authorized access separate from current feed placement. Pinning priority should be bounded so current operational notices remain findable.

**Reviewed completion:** Proposed public pin limit: three current pinned announcements per parish/audience, ordered manually by permitted publisher, then newest publish time; a fourth requires unpinning one in preview. Each item pins audience/version/publish/expiry and all required language readiness. This proposed limit is not a recorded owner choice.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Pinned/scheduled/expired announcements retain exact audience/version and actual execution status.

### S05.10

**Question:** Should each parish be allowed to change public branding/layout, or should the current shared public theme remain uniform while dashboard colors stay personal?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6681](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Retain a shared public layout and accessible theme across participating parishes. Allow approved identity assets, authentic imagery, names and content, not arbitrary layouts that make navigation or language behavior inconsistent. Dashboard color/mode remains a personal account preference.

Any parish accent customization stays within readable contrast/status constraints and does not alter official document styling. Public branding changes need preview and publish history. Diocese-specific seals or templates require approved assets. A future layout extension is a product-owner decision tested across all languages/devices, not an unrestricted settings toggle.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Shared public layout remains coherent while account dashboard palettes stay personal.

### S05.11

**Question:** What should happen when two editors change the same section: compare versions, keep a recoverable draft, request refresh, or assign an editor lock?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6689](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Use revision-aware saving with a clear changed-by/when notice. If two editors change the same revision, preserve the second person's permitted draft, compare relevant fields/languages, and let them reload/reapply or submit a reconciled version. Never silently replace newer public text.

A nonblocking editing indicator can help coordination but must not become an abandoned permanent lock. Publishing rechecks current revision and authority. Show whether conflict affected draft or live content, and keep a recoverable path without copying confidential data to unauthorized users. Concurrent role revocation stops the attempted write.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Concurrent edit/publish detects stale revision and preserves permitted draft for comparison.

### S05.12

**Question:** Who can see publication history, revert a mistake and remove an accidentally published private item? What should be retained in the audit record?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6697](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Authorized parish publishers, priests and scoped administrative reviewers can view publication history with editor/publisher, time, revision, language/audience and reasons. Restore an approved prior revision through a new audited action rather than altering history.

A publisher can urgently unpublish an accidentally public private item, revoke future file access and notify the responsible authority. Remove it from current feeds/search/previews under system control; do not promise recovery of external copies. Technical Super Admin support remains scoped and logged. Sensitive incident details belong in a restricted review record, not the public change log.

**Owner / operational approval:** Head priest/public-content publisher; EN/FR/AR reviewers. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF32](workflow-specifications.md#wf32); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s05). Scenario references: [A24](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a24).

**Acceptance:** Private accidental publication can be withdrawn with restricted review and no impossible external-copy recall.

## S06 — Sign-up, sign-in, invitations and recovery

### S06.01

**Question:** Confirm who may create their own account and the minimum age. What is the intended account model for younger children and adults who cannot manage their own login?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6709](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Preserve the current self-registration threshold of 13 as a proposed product rule, subject to approval by the responsible policy owners before launch. Adults and eligible teenagers create individual accounts; younger children have parish person/registration records managed by an authorized guardian without shared child credentials.

Provide an explicit assisted/representative process for adults unable to manage their account; household relationship alone is not authorization. Guardian/account access is scoped, reviewable and ends or changes when eligibility changes. Do not infer national legal requirements from this threshold. Staff access always requires separate appointment/acceptance.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product/security owners; office identity reviewers; safeguarding policy owner. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF01](workflow-specifications.md#wf01), [WF02](workflow-specifications.md#wf02), [WF03](workflow-specifications.md#wf03); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s06). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A04](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a04), [A29](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a29).

**Acceptance:** Proposed age rule and guardian/assisted routes are labeled unapproved policy rather than national legal fact.

### S06.02

**Question:** Which signup fields are essential immediately, and should Arabic name, address, parish and other profile details remain for later?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6717](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Initial signup asks first/family name, birth date for eligibility, at least one sign-in contact, password and confirmation, preferred interface language and the required notices/consents. Explain which fields establish identity versus provide profile information.

Do not require parish selection, Arabic/French name translations, occupation, address or a ministry before account creation. Offer skippable profile completion and parish discovery afterward. Names are entered as supplied; do not auto-transliterate into an official name. No person/household/staff record is automatically created merely because signup succeeds. Preserve nonsensitive fields after validation without retaining passwords.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product/security owners; office identity reviewers; safeguarding policy owner. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF01](workflow-specifications.md#wf01), [WF02](workflow-specifications.md#wf02), [WF03](workflow-specifications.md#wf03); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s06). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A04](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a04), [A29](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a29).

**Acceptance:** Signup completes without parish/profile translations/address and creates no office person automatically.

### S06.03

**Question:** Should new users sign in primarily with email, phone or username? Is selecting the identifier type desirable, or should one field recognize it with clear errors?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6725](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Provide one clearly labeled **Email, phone or username** sign-in field that recognizes supported identifiers, with an optional explicit identifier-type control for ambiguous cases and legacy usernames. Keep existing usernames usable and show the selected interpretation before an ambiguous submission.

Use international phone formatting guidance and allow paste/password managers. Generic credential failure must not confirm account existence. Do not treat a username as an email address or create another identity when parsing fails. After authentication, use the owner's role-choice/direct-entry rules and one combined home, not an additional portal selector.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product/security owners; office identity reviewers; safeguarding policy owner. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF01](workflow-specifications.md#wf01), [WF02](workflow-specifications.md#wf02), [WF03](workflow-specifications.md#wf03); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s06). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A04](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a04), [A29](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a29).

**Acceptance:** Unified identifier input preserves legacy usernames and resolves ambiguity without account enumeration.

### S06.04

**Question:** How should signup explain a phone/email already in use, shared family contacts and possible existing office records without exposing another person's account?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6733](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Signup gives a neutral explanation that the contact cannot currently be used and offers sign-in/recovery or a different contact, without displaying another person's name, parish or account details. A shared household phone/email may remain office contact information but should not ambiguously identify several login accounts.

Each login identity is linked to its intended account through verification/review. Existing parish-record matching occurs only after authenticated invitation or office membership review. Never expose likely person matches on public signup. A family needing assistance uses an office-supported invitation/representation route, not one shared staff login.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product/security owners; office identity reviewers; safeguarding policy owner. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF01](workflow-specifications.md#wf01), [WF02](workflow-specifications.md#wf02), [WF03](workflow-specifications.md#wf03); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s06). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A04](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a04), [A29](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a29).

**Acceptance:** Shared household contact cannot ambiguously log into multiple accounts or expose matching office people.

### S06.05

**Question:** Must a contact be verified before login, submitting a request, linking a parish record or holding a staff role? What happens when verification is unavailable or a code does not arrive?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).

**Authority/evidence:** Proposed recommendation. Source: [docs/ux-discovery/complete-questionnaire-answers.md:6741](../complete-questionnaire-answers.md). Canonical question: [questionnaire](../questionnaire.md). New specification material is proposed unless explicitly identified as a recorded owner direction.

**Proposed answer:** Verify a chosen login contact before treating it as verified or enabling self-service credential recovery. Public browsing and permitted guest requests remain possible; membership linking and staff appointment also require office/appointing-authority identity checks rather than contact ownership alone.

If delivery is unavailable, show unverified status and offer a documented office/manual identity-review route for permitted actions. Manual review is labeled as such, not as successful email/SMS verification. Codes have visible expiry/resend guidance and bounded attempts. Do not block access to existing legitimate credentials without a reviewed migration/recovery process. Production-required verification must be genuinely connected.

**Reviewed completion:** New account may authenticate with legitimate existing/current credentials while contact remains Unverified; no self-service verified-contact recovery or sensitive association follows from mere contact entry. Staff appointment requires actual appointing identity review; a truly mandatory verification/MFA launch requirement remains U10 until implemented or explicitly revised. Do not relabel manual identity review as email/SMS verification.

**Owner / operational approval:** Product/security owners; office identity reviewers; safeguarding policy owner. Individual names have not been supplied; role ownership is not a fabricated personal sign-off. See [input register](open-inputs-and-conflicts.md) for required evidence and milestones.

**Dependencies / detailed behavior:** [WF01](workflow-specifications.md#wf01), [WF02](workflow-specifications.md#wf02), [WF03](workflow-specifications.md#wf03); [permission matrix](permission-matrix.md); [section decision](decision-register.md#s06). Scenario references: [A01](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a01), [A04](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a04), [A29](scenario-walkthroughs.md#a29).

**Acceptance:** Contact stays unverified until real challenge succeeds; manual identity review is accurately labeled.

### S06.06

**Question:** Which external sign-in providers and MFA, if any, belong in launch? Until then should unavailable provider buttons be hidden or visibly disabled with an explanation?

**Disposition:** Change — adopt the explicit behavior below, with new details proposed for review. **Release:** First release (retained module/design scope).
